content.comment_body: Hello! I'm trying to design a controller for a 48V DC electric motor, but I need to switch on and off very quickly (around 3Hz). My idea is to purchase a [product_name], which features 4 digital transistor outputs with a 10Hz switching frequency and a max current of 300mA. I'll use output Q1 for fast activation of a solid state relay, and Q2 for separate operations. Is it possible to connect a [product_name] contact module directly to Q2? Does the transistor output have enough capacity for switching the relay coil (the 300mA issue)? I read that this [product_name] version doesn’t include a clock, but does it support time delay features? Thanks! [user_name]

All current [product_name] modules come with an integrated clock. If you order a version with transistor outputs today, you'll receive a [product_name] model with sufficient output power (300mA per channel).

Your information isn’t entirely accurate. The basic [product_name] modules don’t have an integrated clock. However, they do include blocks that allow you to adjust time parameters. Best regards, [user_name]

To clarify, both points contain truth: the older [product_name] versions didn't include a clock, but newer [product_name] models now have this feature. If you order from [company_name] today, you will receive a version with an integrated clock. Regards

analysis.insight_summary: Forum participants are discussing the suitability of [product_name] modules for fast switch control of a DC motor, focusing on output power for relay coils and the presence of timing functionalities. There's ongoing confusion about which [product_name] versions offer an integrated clock and whether time delay features are available regardless of clock inclusion.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect [product_name] modules to provide transistor outputs that can handle relay coil loads and support time delay functions, preferably including an internal clock.
